```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
library(bayesmokken)
```

```{r fits, include = FALSE}
data(classroom_wb)
items <- paste0("wb", 1:6)
sup <- bm_supports(classroom_wb, items = items)
f_resp  <- bm_cached("cwb_respondent")
f_equal <- bm_cached("cwb_equal_cluster")
iv_r <- bm_interval(f_resp)
iv_e <- bm_interval(f_equal)
info <- bm_cluster_info(classroom_wb$class_id, data = classroom_wb[, items])
```

When respondents are nested in clusters, two things must be settled that were
never in question before: **which** population quantity is being estimated, and
**how** uncertainty is generated. This vignette does both, and it also records
why the way uncertainty was generated in version 0.9.0 was replaced.

## Two estimands, not one estimand and one nuisance

At the population level, let $M$ be cluster size and $F$ a cluster's response
distribution. The respondent target is the size-weighted mixture
$F_{\mathrm{resp}}=E(MF)/E(M)$; the equal-cluster target is
$F_{\mathrm{eq}}=E(F)$. The former corresponds to sampling a respondent
uniformly. The latter corresponds to sampling a cluster uniformly and then a
respondent uniformly within that cluster.

In a finite sample, write $g = 1, \dots, G$ for clusters and $m_g$ for the size
of cluster $g$, so $n = \sum_g m_g$. The plug-in coefficients use cluster
weights

$$H_{\text{resp}} : \ \omega_g = \frac{m_g}{n},
\qquad\qquad
H_{\text{eq}} : \ \omega_g = \frac{1}{G} .$$

These are sample plug-ins for the two population mixtures, not definitions of
those population distributions. Under equal cluster sizes the plug-ins
coincide. Under **informative cluster size** — when $m_g$ is associated with
the response distribution — they need not.

```{r informative}
data.frame(
  clusters          = info$G,
  respondents       = info$N,
  smallest_cluster  = min(info$sizes),
  largest_cluster   = max(info$sizes),
  informative_index = round(info$informative_index, 3)
)
```

```{r fig-clusters, fig.alt = "Classrooms ordered by size with the weight each target assigns to each: respondent weighting increases with class size while equal-cluster weighting stays flat."}
bm_plot_clusters(classroom_wb$class_id, show_targets = TRUE)
```

```{r targets-differ}
c(respondent = iv_r$point_estimate, equal_cluster = iv_e$point_estimate,
  difference = iv_r$point_estimate - iv_e$point_estimate)
```

That difference is
`r fmt_h(abs(iv_r$point_estimate - iv_e$point_estimate), 4)` here. It is not
sampling error and it does not shrink with $n$. Because neither is more correct
than the other, `cluster_target` has no default, and omitting it is an error
rather than a silent choice.

```{r no-default, error = TRUE}
bb_mokken_h(classroom_wb[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
            cluster = as.character(classroom_wb$class_id),
            weight_law = "complete_record", draws = 200, seed = 1)
```

## The complete-record bootstrap

Treat each cluster, together with every complete-scale response in it, as one
**record**, and treat the records as the independent sampling units. The
complete-record law draws one Dirichlet vector over the records per draw,

$$(A_1, \dots, A_G) \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(1_G),$$

and reweights the records *without touching their contents*. Per respondent
the weight is

$$w_{gi}^{\text{eq}} = \frac{A_g}{m_g},
\qquad\qquad
w_{gi}^{\text{resp}} = \frac{A_g}{\sum_h m_h A_h},$$

with the respondent normalization recomputed in every draw. The target enters
only through that normalization, and nothing inside a record varies from draw
to draw: the variation of responses within a sampled cluster is already part
of what the cluster-level influence values carry, so adding more of it would
count it twice.

### Independent oracle: the seeded complete-record stream

The package generates these weights from the stream used by the clustered
article's replication archive: every draw consumes $G + n$ unit exponentials
from one L'Ecuyer-CMRG stream, the first $G$ are normalized into $A$, and the
remaining $n$ (the archive's within-record block, used there only by the
historical comparator) are discarded. The oracle below reimplements that
stream without calling any package helper, in blocks of 128 draws, which the
package does not use.

```{r verify-weights}
cluster <- as.character(classroom_wb$class_id)
cluster_info <- bayesmokken:::bm_validate_cluster(cluster)
sizes <- cluster_info$sizes
G <- cluster_info$G
n <- cluster_info$N

oracle_crbb <- function(cluster, draws, seed, target, block = 128L) {
  index <- match(cluster, unique(cluster))
  size <- tabulate(index)
  G <- length(size); N <- length(index)
  old_kind <- RNGkind()
  had_seed <- exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)
  old_seed <- if (had_seed) get(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv) else NULL
  on.exit({
    do.call(RNGkind, as.list(old_kind))
    if (had_seed) {
      assign(".Random.seed", old_seed, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    } else if (exists(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv, inherits = FALSE)) {
      rm(".Random.seed", envir = .GlobalEnv)
    }
  }, add = TRUE)
  RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG", "Inversion", "Rejection")
  set.seed(seed)
  out <- matrix(NA_real_, N, draws)
  done <- 0L
  while (done < draws) {
    b <- min(block, draws - done)
    E <- matrix(stats::rexp((G + N) * b), G + N, b)
    A <- sweep(E[seq_len(G), , drop = FALSE], 2,
               colSums(E[seq_len(G), , drop = FALSE]), "/")
    out[, done + seq_len(b)] <- if (target == "respondent") {
      sweep(A[index, , drop = FALSE], 2, colSums(size * A), "/")
    } else {
      A[index, , drop = FALSE] / size[index]
    }
    done <- done + b
  }
  out
}

crbb_resp <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_crbb_weights(
  cluster_info, draws = 300, seed = 18022, target = "respondent"
)
crbb_eq <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_crbb_weights(
  cluster_info, draws = 300, seed = 18022, target = "equal_cluster"
)
stopifnot(
  identical(crbb_resp$weights, oracle_crbb(cluster, 300, 18022, "respondent")),
  identical(crbb_eq$weights, oracle_crbb(cluster, 300, 18022, "equal_cluster")),
  all(abs(colSums(crbb_resp$weights) - 1) < 1e-14),
  all(abs(colSums(crbb_eq$weights) - 1) < 1e-14),
  all(crbb_resp$weights > 0), all(crbb_eq$weights > 0)
)
c(respondents = n, draws_checked = ncol(crbb_resp$weights), targets_checked = 2)
```

The 300 draws cross the package's internal block boundary at 256 and the
oracle's at 128, so agreement also shows that the stream is draw-major: the
same seed gives the same weights for any block or batch size.

### Metamorphic/invariant check: flat within records, mean substitution recovers the point weights

```{r verify-cluster-mass}
idx <- rep(seq_len(G), sizes)
a <- crbb_eq$record_mass                       # the G x draws outer draws

# Within every record the equal-cluster weights are the record weight divided
# by its size: no second reweighting, for every draw.
flat <- vapply(seq_len(G), function(g) {
  block <- crbb_eq$weights[idx == g, , drop = FALSE]
  max(abs(sweep(block, 2, a[g, ] / sizes[g], "-")))
}, numeric(1))
stopifnot(max(flat) == 0)

# Replacing A by its mean 1/G recovers the plug-in targets exactly.
point_resp <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_point_weights(cluster_info, "respondent")
point_eq <- bayesmokken:::bm_cluster_point_weights(cluster_info, "equal_cluster")
mean_a <- rep(1 / G, G)
stopifnot(
  max(abs(mean_a[idx] / sum(sizes * mean_a) - point_resp)) < 1e-15,
  max(abs(mean_a[idx] / sizes[idx] - point_eq)) < 1e-15
)

data.frame(
  size = sizes,
  point_respondent = round(as.numeric(tapply(point_resp, idx, sum)), 4),
  point_equal = round(as.numeric(tapply(point_eq, idx, sum)), 4),
  one_draw_respondent = round(as.numeric(tapply(crbb_resp$weights[, 1], idx, sum)), 4),
  one_draw_equal = round(as.numeric(tapply(crbb_eq$weights[, 1], idx, sum)), 4)
)[order(sizes)[c(1, 2, G - 1, G)], ]
```

The first two mass columns are the finite-sample plug-in targets. The last two
are one random draw, included only to show that realized record masses
fluctuate. No claim is made that their draw-wise average equals the plug-in
target.

## Why the two-stage law was replaced

Version 0.9.0 drew, in addition and independently, a second Dirichlet vector
*within* every record, $(B_{g1}, \dots, B_{g m_g}) \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(1_{m_g})$,
so that the per-respondent weights became $A_g B_{gi}$ and
$m_g A_g B_{gi} / \sum_h m_h A_h$. Substituting mean weights returns the same
plug-in targets under either law, so the two laws are centered on the same
thing. They differ in spread. Conditionally on the data, the complete-record
draws of $H$ have the first-order limit of the sampling distribution of the
coefficient, with variance $\sigma^2$; the two-stage draws have variance
$\sigma^2 + \omega^2$ with

$$\omega^2 = 2\,E\!\left\{\frac{c(M)^2\, v}{M + 1}\right\} \ge 0,$$

where $v$ is the within-record dispersion of the influence values and $c(M)$
the target's size normalization. The extra term is of the same order as
$\sigma^2$ and does not vanish as $G$ grows, so the earlier shrinkage
$1 - 1.5/\sqrt{G}$ — which tends to one — could only patch it over the range on
which it was tuned. The clustered article's current version derives this
(its Proposition on conditional weight-law limits) and measures it: on a
matched series of designs that vary $G$ alone, the two-stage draw variance
exceeded the complete-record draw variance by a factor between 2.5 and 2.6.

### Executable illustration: the two laws on the classroom data

```{r two-laws}
quiet <- function(expr) {
  suppressWarnings(expr, classes = "bm_historical_method_warning")
}
f_two_stage <- quiet(bb_mokken_h(
  classroom_wb[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
  cluster = cluster, cluster_target = "respondent",
  weight_law = "hierarchical_cluster", draws = 2000, seed = 1, warn = FALSE
))
sd_ratio <- stats::sd(f_two_stage$draws$scale) / stats::sd(f_resp$draws$scale)
data.frame(
  law = c("complete_record", "hierarchical_cluster (historical)"),
  draw_sd = round(c(stats::sd(f_resp$draws$scale),
                    stats::sd(f_two_stage$draws$scale)), 4),
  variance_ratio = round(c(1, sd_ratio^2), 2),
  method_id = c(bm_interval(f_resp)$method_id,
                bm_interval(f_two_stage)$method_id)
)
```

Same data, same seed: the two-stage draws are visibly more dispersed. This is
an illustration on one synthetic dataset, not evidence about coverage; the
evidence is in the confirmation summarized below.

## The adjustment

Let $q_L$ and $q_U$ be the type-8 quantiles at .025 and .975 of the defined
complete-record draws and $\hat H$ the point estimate. The percentile interval
$[q_L, q_U]$ inherits the first-order coverage of the law, but with few
clusters it undercovers, so the reported interval acts on the bootstrap
*errors* instead. Reflecting the error quantiles about $\hat H$ gives the basic
interval; expanding the reflected errors by

$$k_G = \sqrt{\frac{G+1}{G-1}}\;\frac{t_{G-1,\,.975}}{z_{.975}}$$

and intersecting with $(-\infty, 1]$ gives the reported one:

$$\bigl[\hat H - k_G\,(q_U - \hat H),\ \hat H - k_G\,(q_L - \hat H)\bigr]
\cap (-\infty, 1].$$

The first factor of $k_G$ matches the conditional Dirichlet variance to the
sampling variance of a linear cluster mean exactly; the second is a
$t$-reference heuristic. Together they are a prespecified function of $G$,
selected between two prespecified candidates before any confirmation outcome
existed, not a constant fitted to data.

**Executable consistency check — reconstruct the reported endpoints from the
stored quantiles, point estimate and $G$.**

```{r verify-adjustment}
k_G <- sqrt((iv_r$cluster_count + 1) / (iv_r$cluster_count - 1)) *
  stats::qt(0.975, iv_r$cluster_count - 1) / stats::qnorm(0.975)
h <- iv_r$point_estimate

stopifnot(
  all.equal(k_G, iv_r$width_multiplier, tolerance = 0),
  all.equal(h - k_G * (iv_r$raw_upper - h), iv_r$reflected_lower, tolerance = 0),
  all.equal(h - k_G * (iv_r$raw_lower - h), iv_r$reflected_upper, tolerance = 0),
  all.equal(min(iv_r$reflected_upper, 1), iv_r$upper, tolerance = 0),
  all.equal(iv_r$reflected_lower, iv_r$lower, tolerance = 0)
)
data.frame(G = iv_r$cluster_count, k_G = k_G,
           binary_multiplier_for_comparison = 1 + 0.25 / sqrt(iv_r$n_complete))
```

The reflection is about the point estimate, not the midpoint of the
percentile interval, so the reported interval need not contain $\hat H$ and
need not share the percentile interval's midpoint. An empty intersection,
which arises only when the lower reflected endpoint exceeds one, is reported
as an empty set with its own status, never as $[1, 1]$.

```{r fig-calibration, fig.alt = "Interval multiplier k_G against the number of clusters: above one, decreasing toward one, solid from 22 through 320 where the confirmation was conducted and dashed outside that range."}
bm_plot_calibration(mode = "clustered")
```

```{r k-table}
Gs <- c(22, 30, 55, 80, 160, 320)
data.frame(G = Gs,
           k_G = round(sqrt((Gs + 1) / (Gs - 1)) * stats::qt(0.975, Gs - 1) /
                         stats::qnorm(0.975), 4))
```

### Cluster counts, and what the validation status says

The procedure is computable for $G \ge 2$. That is a requirement for the
arithmetic, not a recommendation that two clusters support inference. The
confirmation covered cluster counts 22, 30, 35, 55, 80, 160 and 320, and the
object records whether its count lies inside 22–320:

```{r validated-range}
c(status = iv_r$validation_status,
  confirmed_min = iv_r$validated_cluster_min,
  confirmed_max = iv_r$validated_cluster_max,
  this_fit = iv_r$cluster_count)
```

```{r range-outside}
small <- classroom_wb[classroom_wb$class_id %in% levels(classroom_wb$class_id)[1:10], ]
iv_small <- bm_interval(bb_mokken_h(
  small[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
  cluster = as.character(droplevels(small$class_id)),
  cluster_target = "respondent", draws = 300, seed = 1, warn = FALSE
))
c(G = iv_small$cluster_count, k_G = round(iv_small$width_multiplier, 4),
  status = iv_small$validation_status)
```

The historical two-stage lane keeps the refusal that belonged to its
shrinkage, which was confirmed on 22–80 clusters only:

```{r range-refusal, error = TRUE}
quiet(bb_mokken_h(small[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
                  cluster = as.character(droplevels(small$class_id)),
                  cluster_target = "respondent",
                  weight_law = "hierarchical_cluster",
                  draws = 300, seed = 1, interval = "calibrated"))
```

```{r fig-two-stage, fig.alt = "Historical two-stage width multiplier against the number of clusters: below one, increasing toward one, solid from 22 through 80 and dashed outside that range."}
bm_plot_calibration(mode = "clustered_two_stage")
```

## Guard rails

Three combinations are refused outright, because each would apply a procedure
outside the conditions under which it was developed and confirmed.

**Dichotomous items with a cluster argument.** The clustered method was
developed and confirmed on polytomous items. Refused on every route, including
the percentile comparator and the historical lane:

```{r guard-binary, error = TRUE}
data(srs)
bb_mokken_h(srs, cluster = rep(1:25, length.out = nrow(srs)),
            cluster_target = "respondent", draws = 200, seed = 1)
```

**Polytomous items under the independent-respondent law.** Random weights with
no records to reweight:

```{r guard-iid, error = TRUE}
bb_mokken_h(classroom_wb[, items], item_type = "ordinal", supports = sup,
            weight_law = "iid_respondent", draws = 200, seed = 1)
```

**Undeclared supports.** Shown in `vignette("m1-foundations")`; the denominator
would be computed at a support the user never declared.

```{r guardrails}
bm_guardrails()[1:4, c("situation", "what_to_do")]
```

## The evidence

The clustered article's confirmation ran the frozen procedure on 41,000
datasets generated after the freeze: 24 conditions, 21 of them regular, with
cluster counts from 22 to 320, three cluster-size mechanisms (balanced,
size-dependent, and resampled from the SWMDK classrooms), latent intraclass
correlations from 0 to .35, and three stress conditions near or at a
population knot that enter no criterion. Equal-condition coverage over the 21
regular conditions, both targets:

| Procedure | Respondent | Equal-cluster |
|---|---|---|
| **Adjusted complete-record interval (this package's default)** | **.947** | **.949** |
| Complete-record percentile interval (`interval = "equal_tail"`) | .935 | .936 |
| Whole-cluster multinomial resampling, percentile | .939 | .940 |
| Two-stage HBB, raw (the 0.9.0 law before shrinkage) | .997 | .997 |
| Two-stage HBB, shrunk by $1 - 1.5/\sqrt{G}$ (`weight_law = "hierarchical_cluster"`) | .977 | .977 |
| Clustered delta interval of **mokken** (respondent target only) | .984 | — |

The adjusted interval was 6% wider than the percentile interval of the same
draws and 15% narrower than the shrunk two-stage interval. All four
prespecified criteria (coverage equivalence to $[.93, .97]$, each tail at most
.04, operational failure at most .005) were established in 36 of the 42
condition–target assessments; the six that were not are upper-tail criteria
whose one-sided bounds crossed .04 at some small-$G$ conditions, which the
article reports as not established rather than as excess. No condition was
revisited after its outcome existed.

Applied without retuning to the SWMDK school data (639 pupils in 30
classrooms), the procedure produces the intervals shown in
`vignette("a3-clustered-polytomous-workflow")`, and the package reproduces
them at the article's seeds.
